plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets fill with clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers on bare or feathery-leafed branches. The fallen blossoms carpet pavements in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to November, with peak color in late October and early November
plants.location: Australia (Sydney and Brisbane), South Africa (Pretoria) and Argentina (Buenos Aires)
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the tens of thousands of these trees lining its streets. The trees are native to South America and were introduced to South Africa in the 1800s.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Daisy-like flowers sit on slender stems above fine, feathery foliage. Their papery petals sway in the breeze and attract butterflies and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere, and in warm-climate gardens such as Mexico, where it is native and flowers into autumn
plants.location: Mexico and gardens in warm temperate regions of the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word for order or harmony. Spanish priests in Mexico are said to have grown it in mission gardens.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub produces delicate, slightly fragrant blooms as the weather cools. Its petals open wide to show golden stamens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, roughly October to December
plants.location: Japan and the southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the tea plant. Its seeds are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil.
